To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the treatment of wealth and income distribution in the high school economics textbooks is very limited, (2) there are some significant differences in the treatment of the subject among the textbooks, and (3) the textbooks do not present the subject matter in a way that would be most effective in helping high school students understand the nature and causes of wealth distribution.

high school economics texts: (1) devote little space to wealth distribution, (2) present wealth distribution as a problem, (3) present wealth distribution in terms of the poor and the rich, (4) present wealth distribution primarily in terms of income, (5) present the poor as a homogeneous group, (6) do not present the poor as consumers, and (7) do not present any policy recommendations for dealing with the problem.
